name: Dallas
operatingHours: DART light rail runs ~3:45 AM–~1:15 AM daily (every ~15–20 min, ~30 min early, late and on weekends); the Silver Line (opened Oct 2025) runs ~5:00 AM–~11:30 PM. The Dallas Streetcar (Union Station–Bishop Arts) runs ~5:30 AM–midnight, and the free M-Line trolley through Uptown ~7:00 AM–10:00 PM (later Fri–Sat).
fareInfo: A DART 3-Hour Pass is $3.00 and a Local Day Pass $6.00 (2026), covering light rail, the Silver Line, buses and the Dallas Streetcar, including trips to DFW Airport; a Regional Day Pass (adds Trinity Railway Express and Denton/Fort Worth services) is $9. Buy in the GoPass app, at station ticket machines, or tap a contactless bank card/phone at the validators. The M-Line trolley is free.

sights.name: The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza
sights.note: Exhibits on President Kennedy's life and 1963 assassination, inside the former Texas School Book Depository where the shots were fired.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Wed–Sun (last entry 4:15 PM), closed Mon & Tue

sights.name: Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Gardens
sights.note: 66 acres of themed gardens on the shore of White Rock Lake, famous for spring tulips and the autumn pumpkin village.

sights.name: The Dallas World Aquarium
sights.note: A walk-through rainforest and aquarium in the West End, with sloths, toucans, manatees and a shark tunnel.

sights.name: Reunion Tower
sights.note: The lit-up geodesic ball on the skyline; the GeO-Deck observation level gives 360° views 470 ft above downtown.
sights.hours: ~12:30–8:30 PM most days (from ~3:30 PM Tue–Wed, to ~10:00 PM Sat); last elevator 30 min before close

sights.name: George W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum
sights.note: The 43rd president's museum on the SMU campus, with a full-size Oval Office replica and a 9/11 gallery.

sights.name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
sights.note: Five floors of hands-on science, dinosaur skeletons and gems inside a striking concrete cube in Victory Park.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM (Sun from 11:00 AM), closed Tue except Nov–Dec

sights.name: Dallas Museum of Art
sights.note: A broad free-entry collection spanning ancient Americas to Monet and Pollock, anchoring the Arts District.
sights.hours: 11:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue–Sun (to 9:00 PM Thu), closed Mon

sights.name: Dealey Plaza
sights.note: The 1930s plaza where JFK was shot; an X on Elm Street and the grassy knoll draw visitors around the clock.

sights.name: Dallas Zoo
sights.note: Texas's oldest and largest zoo, with a giraffe-feeding deck and a big African savanna; on the DART Red Line.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (9:00 AM–4:00 PM from early Nov and in midsummer)

sights.name: Pioneer Plaza Cattle Drive
sights.note: Forty-nine bronze longhorns and three cowboys drive across a hillside park beside the Convention Center.

sights.name: Klyde Warren Park
sights.note: A lawn-and-plaza deck built over a sunken freeway, with food trucks, games and free events between Uptown and the Arts District.

sights.name: Bishop Arts District
sights.note: Oak Cliff's walkable grid of indie boutiques, bakeries, bars and murals, reached by the Dallas Streetcar.
sights.hours: Streets always open; most shops ~11:00 AM–7:00 PM, restaurants later

sights.name: Frontiers of Flight Museum
sights.note: Aviation and spaceflight history at Love Field, including the Apollo 7 capsule and early Southwest Airlines jets.

sights.name: White Rock Lake Park
sights.note: A large city lake with a 9-mile loop trail for walking and cycling, and sunset views back to the skyline.

sights.name: Dallas Holocaust and Human Rights Museum
sights.note: A moving modern museum in the West End tracing the Holocaust and the American civil-rights struggle.

sights.name: Nasher Sculpture Center
sights.note: A Renzo Piano gallery and garden of modern sculpture by Rodin, Calder, Moore and Serra.

sights.name: Deep Ellum
sights.note: Former warehouse district east of downtown, now Dallas's live-music, mural and bar strip; liveliest after dark.
sights.hours: Streets always open; bars and venues mostly evenings until 2:00 AM

sights.name: Dallas Farmers Market
sights.note: Covered food hall and weekend produce shed in the Farmers Market district, good for a casual lunch.
sights.hours: Market hall ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM daily; outdoor Shed weekends ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM

railStations.name: Dallas Union Station
railStations.note: Amtrak's Texas Eagle (Chicago–San Antonio–Los Angeles) stops here once daily each way; Trinity Railway Express commuter trains run to Fort Worth (~1 hr) via CentrePort for DFW. DART Red and Blue Lines and the Dallas Streetcar stop at the station.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM; Texas Eagle runs one train each way daily, TRE weekdays every ~30–60 min and reduced Saturdays, no Sunday service.

airports.name: DFW Airport
airports.transitNote: DART Orange Line (shown on map) runs from DFW Airport Station at Terminal A to downtown West End in ~50 min for the $3 local fare; the Silver Line (also on map) serves DFW Airport Terminal B station toward Addison, Richardson and Plano. Use the free Skylink train to change terminals.
airports.hours: Orange Line: first train ~3:50 AM, last to downtown ~1:10 AM (earlier ~12:10 AM weekends).

airports.name: Dallas Love Field
airports.transitNote: The DART Love Link shuttle bus (~10 min) links the terminal to Inwood/Love Field station on the Green and Orange Lines (shown on map), then ~15 min to downtown; the whole trip uses one $3 pass. Taxi or rideshare to downtown is ~15 min.
airports.hours: Love Link shuttle ~5:00 AM–~midnight; trains from Inwood/Love Field until ~1:00 AM.
